data.body: `resolve_config_revision` interpolates the caller-supplied `path` directly into a shell command string and runs it via `subprocess.run(command, shell=True, ...)`. Any path containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, backticks, `$()`, etc.) is executed as part of the shell invocation, giving arbitrary command execution (CWE-78). The value flows straight from `argv[1]` in `main`, so it is attacker-controlled input. Build the argv list explicitly and drop `shell=True` so the path is always treated as a single literal argument.
